evergreen_facts.text: São Paulo was founded by Jesuit missionaries, among them José de Anchieta, on 25 January 1554.
Prince Pedro declared Brazil's independence beside the Ipiranga brook in São Paulo on 7 September 1822.
São Paulo grew rapidly in the 19th century on the wealth of coffee farmed across the surrounding state.
São Paulo's Liberdade district is the heart of Brazil's large Japanese-Brazilian community.
The 1922 Modern Art Week at São Paulo's Municipal Theatre helped launch Brazilian modernism.
The São Paulo Museum of Art, designed by Lina Bo Bardi, is lifted above Avenida Paulista on two huge red beams.
São Paulo's Ibirapuera Park, opened in 1954, has pavilions and an auditorium designed by Oscar Niemeyer.
The Municipal Theatre of São Paulo, an ornate opera house in the city center, opened in 1911.
São Paulo's Municipal Market, opened in 1933, is famous for its stained glass and towering mortadella sandwiches.
São Paulo's Pacaembu Stadium, opened in 1940, is home to the Museu do Futebol, a museum of Brazilian football.
The Interlagos circuit in São Paulo has hosted Formula One's Brazilian Grand Prix since the 1970s.
Ayrton Senna, three-time Formula One world champion, was born in São Paulo in 1960.
São Paulo sits on a plateau about 760 metres above sea level, inland from the Atlantic coast.
The Tietê River runs through São Paulo and flows inland, away from the nearby Atlantic Ocean.
The Serra do Mar mountains, cloaked in Atlantic Forest, separate São Paulo's plateau from the coast.
São Paulo's Butantan Institute, founded in 1901, is a biomedical research center known for snake antivenoms.
